transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-10
Time: 16:00 - 16:54 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ross (Redwood SE), Lena Cho (Redwood SE), Oliver Ng (Guava Head of Search), Priya Menon (ML Engineer), Diego Ramirez (CTO), Samira Khan (Product)
Links shared: demo slides https://redwood.app/decks/guava-concierge, pilot sheet https://redwood.app/pilots/guava-2026, benchmark template (sheet) https://redwood.app/benchmarks/guava

Quick summary (auto): walked through Hosted API embeddings flow, demonstrated rerank endpoint for reorder use-case, showed Console suggestions from Optimize, discussed data retention and KMS. Pilot agreed.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood -- i'm the AE on this account, and with me today are Ethan and lena from our solutions engineering team. how are you all?
[00:08] Oliver Ng: hey thanks, doing good. excited to see how this could plug into our concierge search product, we have about 50k docs in initial phase.
[00:15] Priya Menon: hi all, quick background — we currently index embeddings in-house, we use an opensearch + vector plugin and Pinecone for some pro types, but looking to simplify and lower latencies for re-rank stage.
[00:28] Ethan Ross: great, that's helpful context. we'll focus on two things: the embeddings endpoint and our dedicated rerank/reorder endpoint that runs a light cross-attention reranker, plus show how Console Optimize suggests batching/quantization settings.
[00:42] Diego Ramirez: quick question on cost — we care about ops cost per query, we run ~200 qps at peak for the concierge flow, and average latency targets are sub-250ms for the rerank. is that realistic?
[00:55] Lena Cho: mm-hmm, good note. for hosted we can target that with small model variants and continuous batching; the rerank endpoint is optimized for short context cross-attention, so typical 50-100 candidate reranks can be in the 150-300ms range depending on model and concurrency.
[01:12] Maya Patel: i'll show the Console shortly; but to address the ops piece — Optimize gives suggestions: reduce dimensionality of embeddings per workload, warm prefix caches for popular queries, and set batching windows to balance latency vs throughput.
[01:27] Oliver Ng: when you say "prefix caches" is that like KV cache for decoder states? we are worried about cold-starts for burst traffic.
[01:36] Ethan Ross: good question — two things: for generation KV cache matters, but for embeddings+rerank we use a combination of query cache for embeddings and a prefix hotcache for frequent candidates; we also support sticky routing to reduce coldness. sometimes transcription here mislabels words but the idea is pre-warming.
[01:55] Samira Khan: can you walk through an example: we send a user query, we do vector search to return top 200, and then rerank to top 5. what endpoints do we call and what does the payload look like?
[02:06] Lena Cho: absolutely — flow is: call /v1/embeddings (hosted) with batched documents to build index, or you can upload precomputed vectors; query time you call /v1/embeddings for the query, run similarity search in your store (or use Redwood's built-in retriever if you want), then call /v1/rerank with the query + candidate texts (or candidate ids + vectors) — we demo passing text candidates in this session. payload is small but we compress the candidate list and we recommend gzipped payload for 200 candidates.
[02:30] Priya Menon: do you recommend storing vectors in our own store or use Redwood's embedding store? we have a bunch of existing infra and we are sensitive to vendor lock-in.
[02:38] Ethan Ross: we support either. many teams keep vectors in their existing index (OpenSearch, Faiss, etc.) and call Redwood for the query embedding + rerank. others use Redwood's managed vector store for convenience; Optimize will analyze your workload and recommend whichever yields better token cost + latency.
[02:55] Oliver Ng: what about model selection — we have ~100 tokens per rerank candidate, so the model choice affects both cost and latency. any guidance?
[03:05] Lena Cho: for rerank we recommend mid-size encoder-decoder reranker variants; for hosted we expose a model catalog with performance profiles. in the Console i can show you a profile that maps candidate count to expected p95 latency and token cost.
[03:20] Maya Patel: let me share my screen and run a quick demo — slide deck first, then live calls to the hosted endpoints.
[03:28] [screen share starts]
[03:30] Maya Patel: slide one — goals: reduce median time-to-first-result, improve top-5 relevance, and cut per-query cost by 30%.
[03:40] Oliver Ng: those numbers look right. how do you measure "top-5 relevance" in your platform?
[03:44] Ethan Ross: we tie it to evals and quality monitoring — you upload labeled query sets, Redwood runs A/B comparisons across model versions and surfaces regression alerts in Console. it's integrated with the rollout tools so you can canary newer reranker variants.
[04:00] [00:04:00] Maya Patel: now a live run — i'm going to call the embeddings endpoint with a sample query to show how compact the response is.
[04:10] [00:04:10] Maya (API): POST /v1/embeddings {"input": ["best restaurants in seattle"]} -> returns 1 vector (dim 1536) and metadata.
[04:22] Priya Menon: are embeddings deterministic across runs? we need reproducibility for offline replays.
[04:28] Ethan Ross: yes, we offer deterministic seeding options for certain model families; there's also an "embed_version" field to pin to a particular model+tokenizer combo.
[04:35] [00:04:35] Oliver Ng: how about latency to compute embeddings — if we call for each user query, how much overhead?
[04:42] Lena Cho: small — typical single-query embedding compute is sub-30ms on hosted for our optimized encoders, but depends on batch and region. we recommend batching many document ingests but compute embeddings per query for freshness.
[04:55] Maya Patel: switching to rerank: i'm calling /v1/rerank with one query and 100 text candidates — watch the response.
[05:05] [00:05:05] Maya (API): POST /v1/rerank {"query": "best brunch near downtown", "candidates": [...] } -> returns scored candidate list, top-N.
[05:18] Samira Khan: that response came back in ~220ms — nice. does Redwood supply the scoring function or do you return embeddings similarity?
[05:26] Ethan Ross: we return model-based scores and a confidence metric; you can also request feature-level explanations (at extra token cost) for top results.
[05:36] Oliver Ng: are the rerank calls stateful? e.g., can they reference a document id and fetch vector server-side?
[05:44] Lena Cho: yes, you can pass candidate ids and we will retrieve vectors server-side if you host them with Redwood; otherwise include text or precomputed vectors.
[05:53] Diego Ramirez: for our SLA we need audit logs of user queries and redaction — what's available?
[05:59] Maya Patel: hosted can provide audit trails, user token mapping, and you can enable redaction rules that strip PII before storage. for Private we have more controls but hosted still supports KMS-backed encryption at rest and SSO.
[06:12] [00:06:12] Priya Menon: what about retention windows and ability to delete data on demand for compliance?
[06:18] Ethan Ross: retention is configurable per-tenant; we also support programmatic purge endpoints and supply deletion certificates for audits.
[06:27] Oliver Ng: that helps. also curious about throughput — if we run a pilot with 5k concurrent users, what should we expect?
[06:35] Lena Cho: depends on candidate set and model. Optimize will profile your traffic and suggest dedicated vs hosted capacity. for 5k concurrent light reranks you probably want a Hybrid Dedicated pool, but for pilot hosted usually suffices.
[06:48] Samira Khan: what does a Hybrid Dedicated pool mean?
[06:51] Maya Patel: it's basically a reserved capacity for your account with burst-on-hosted capability — so you get predictable throughput but avoid upfront on-prem investment.
[07:02] [00:07:02] Oliver Ng: any examples of customers who moved from hosted -> dedicated? cost delta?
[07:09] Ethan Ross: yes, we had a marketplace company move to Dedicated after 6 months; they cut per-query cost by ~40% at scale due to quantization + custom batching. we can share anonymized numbers in the pricing sheet.
[07:22] Priya Menon: can Optimize recommend quantization levels automatically? we worry about quality drop.
[07:29] Lena Cho: yes, Optimize runs evals and can recommend Q4_0 or Q4_1 depending on your quality threshold. it ties recommendations to eval sets so you can see expected metric delta before applying.
[07:42] Maya Patel: i'm going to switch to the Console to show the Optimize tab — you can upload eval sets, run A/B, and we surface cost/latency tradeoff curves.
[07:53] [screen share: Console]
[07:55] Maya Patel: here's the model catalog; you can see p50/p95 latencies and token costs per model. we also show rerank-specific profiles for candidate counts.
[08:06] Oliver Ng: oh that candidate chart is handy — shows 50/200/500 candidate latencies.
[08:10] Ethan Ross: yeah and you can pin a model version for rollout, or configure canary percentages to slowly shift traffic.
[08:20] Samira Khan: for the pilot we want reproducible bench numbers — will you run a benchmark with our sample docs?
[08:26] Maya Patel: yes — action: you share 50k docs and we run embedding + rerank benchmark using your query templates; we'll produce a sheet with p50/p95 cost and latency.
[08:36] [00:08:36] Priya Menon: what's included in the pilot — is it just calls or do you also ingest and host vectors?
[08:44] Lena Cho: pilot can include both ingestion into Redwood's managed store and calling rerank. we'll tailor to your stack; no lock-in, you can export vectors afterwards.
[08:57] Oliver Ng: security — can you do SSO and SCIM? we need provisioned users and RBAC.
[09:05] Ethan Ross: yes SSO (SAML/OIDC) + SCIM provisioning, per-route RBAC, audit logs, and optional private deployments for stricter compliance.
[09:14] Diego Ramirez: KMS integration? we use AWS KMS for keys.
[09:18] Maya Patel: supported — we integrate with customer KMS (AWS/Azure/GCP) for Private and offer envelope encryption for Hosted with Bring Your Own Key options.
[09:28] Priya Menon: curious about fallback behavior — if a model variant is overloaded, will request be rerouted to a cheaper model or queue?
[09:36] Lena Cho: Smart routing — policy-based. you can configure latency-first or cost-first policies; when capacity constrained requests can fall back to a cheaper variant or route to another region.
[09:48] [00:09:48] Oliver Ng: are those policies per-route? we have several search endpoints with different SLAs.
[09:54] Ethan Ross: yes per-route and per-model. you can set SLOs per-route in Console and Redwood will try to satisfy them with configured fallbacks.
[10:03] Samira Khan: about model drift — how do you monitor relevance over time?
[10:07] Maya Patel: two parts: continuous quality monitoring (we compare production outputs to your eval queries) and rollout controls that can auto-rollback if a new model causes regression.
[10:18] Priya Menon: ok good. can you show the rerank payload size limits? we sometimes hit 1MB per request.
[10:25] Lena Cho: hosted has a soft 2MB payload recommendation; for large candidate sets we recommend server-side ids+vectors or chunked rerank flows. also gzipping helps.
[10:36] Oliver Ng: what's the recommended candidate pipeline for best quality/cost tradeoff?
[10:41] Ethan Ross: typical: coarse filter with vector search to top 500, cheap lexical or recency filter to 200, move to rerank model for top 50, then final re-score combining business signals.
[10:54] [00:10:54] Diego Ramirez: can we return additional features from rerank to feed personalization layer?
[10:59] Lena Cho: yes, you can request metadata & feature vectors with the score; note this increases token usage and potential cost.
[11:10] Samira Khan: any considerations for multi-lingual queries — we have a global userbase.
[11:15] Ethan Ross: we have multilingual embedding models; Optimize will surface per-language latency and accuracy differences and recommend model variants per region.
[11:26] Oliver Ng: ok, good. let's talk about pilot success criteria — what should we measure?
[11:32] Maya Patel: measure top-5 relevance lift vs baseline, p95 latency under synthetic load, and cost per active user. agreed thresholds and we'll bake into the pilot sheet.
[11:40] Priya Menon: can you include human evals in that sheet? we prefer some human-labeled QA.
[11:45] Lena Cho: yes, we support human-in-the-loop evals and can aggregate judgments in Console.
[11:51] [00:11:51] Maya Patel: i'm going to show a quick canary roll — selecting 5% of traffic to new rerank model and watching rollout metrics.
[11:58] [screen: Canary rollout chart]
[12:02] Oliver Ng: looks solid. on the cost side, send us a 12-month forecast for expected volume and cost-breakdown.
[12:10] Maya Patel: will do — i'll include token, storage, and dedicated pool options.
[12:16] Diego Ramirez: latency consistency is our #1, cost is #2. are there guarantees?
[12:22] Ethan Ross: for Dedicated we offer SLA-backed p95 windows; hosted has soft SLOs but you can opt into reserved capacity.
[12:31] Samira Khan: about data locality — can we pin region to EU only?
[12:38] Lena Cho: yes, hosted supports region pinning for data residency; Private deployments give even more control.
[12:46] [00:12:46] Priya Menon: any gotchas when switching from our current hybrid—we use pinecone for vectors and an internal reranker — latency varies a lot.
[12:56] Maya Patel: common pitfalls: not batching document ingests, not pinning hot shards, and leaving default batching windows. Optimize typically finds these and suggests changes.
[13:06] Oliver Ng: what's the timeline for pilot setup? we want to start next week.
[13:10] Ethan Ross: we can provision test keys and a sandbox in 48 hours; full pilot with managed ingestion typically 5 business days after data receipt.
[13:18] Maya Patel: i'll follow up with the pilot doc and the pricing sheet.
[13:22] [00:13:22] Priya Menon: on the technical side we'll verify reproducibility and run baseline A/B.
[13:28] Samira Khan: ok — any final security items we should raise?
[13:33] Diego Ramirez: SOC 2 + FedRAMP? we may need higher compliance later.
[13:38] Lena Cho: hosted supports SOC 2; for FedRAMP-level we advise Private/on-prem or dedicated FedRAMP partners.
[13:46] Oliver Ng: we also need to know egress costs if vector storage moves to Redwood.
[13:52] Maya Patel: noted — we'll include that in the cost breakdown.
[14:00] [00:14:00] Maya Patel: wrapping up — agree on next steps: we run a 1-week pilot with your 50k docs, Redwood runs benchmark and returns results, + pricing & security deck.
[14:10] Oliver Ng: yep sounds good. thanks for the practical demo.
[14:14] Priya Menon: thanks everyone.
[14:18] Maya Patel: i'll send meeting notes and action items. thanks all.
[14:22] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription missed a couple of technical terms (e.g., exact model variant names) and occasionally conflated "rerank" with "re-radar" in a couple places; quality flagged as medium.
